argument_markdown:
## Source-backed and verified inputs

The geometric input is exactly the dependency ATT-0112 as dual-confirmed by REV-0157 and REV-0158. In particular, CLM-0112-2 supplies the smooth reduced balanced base, CLM-0112-6 excludes a component contained in the type-(ii) locus, CLM-0112-7 supplies the balanced quotient-stack geometry, and CLM-0112-8 gives full S_6 monodromy and connectedness of the ordering torsor on a smooth atlas. These artifacts do not assert any Tate property.

From the established balanced Casnati–Ekedahl calculation, h^0(L_s)=3 on every geometric fibre. Grauert is used only over the stated reduced base, so p_*L is locally free of rank three and A=P_S(p_*L) is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle. The packet facts FND-0165, FND-0166, and FND-0167 supply the rational compact-support transfer and lowest-weight open-immersion statements used below. FND-0033 supplies semisimplicity of pure polarizable rational Hodge structures.

## Proved steps

1. Because Z→U is a finite étale S_6-torsor and the coefficients are rational, averaging is exact and gives Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U;Q)=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)^{S_6}=M_[6].

2. Apply FND-0165 to the open immersion U⊂A. It gives an injection Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U;Q)→Gr^W_16 H_c^16(A;Q). The projective-bundle formula for the P^2-bundle A→S identifies the target with Gr^W_16 H_c^16(S;Q)⊕Gr^W_14 H_c^14(S;Q)(-1)⊕Gr^W_12 H_c^12(S;Q)(-2). This proves the first displayed injection.

3. Put Z^(1)=Z/S_5, where S_5 fixes the first label. Rational transfer gives Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z^(1);Q)=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)^{S_5}. By the S_6-to-S_5 branching rule, only V_[6] and V_[5,1] have S_5-invariants, each with multiplicity one; hence this Hodge structure is M_[6]⊕M_[5,1]. By FND-0166, Z^(1) is the reduced-support open in the universal divisor 𝒟, and 𝒟→𝒞 is a Zariski-locally trivial P^1-bundle. FND-0165 followed by the P^1-bundle formula therefore gives the second displayed injection.

4. Under the stated hypothesis on S, every summand in the target of the first injection is a sum of Q(-8), since Q(-7)(-1)=Q(-8) and Q(-6)(-2)=Q(-8). Semisimplicity makes M_[6] a sum of Q(-8). Duality between Gr^W_16 H_c^16 and W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}, with no additional twist, gives T_16(U)=T_16(Z)^{S_6} as a sum of Q(8).

5. Under the stated hypothesis on 𝒞, both summands in the target of the second injection are sums of Q(-8). Thus M_[6] and M_[5,1] are sums of Q(-8), and their dual [6]- and [5,1]-isotypic Borel–Moore pieces are sums of Q(8).

## Computational hypotheses

None. No finite experiment or point count is used.

## Gaps

The constant-coefficient Tate hypotheses on S and 𝒞 are not proved by ATT-0112, REV-0157, REV-0158, or the packet. The remaining S_6-isotypic multiplicity spaces are uncontrolled; FND-0164 prevents replacing this missing work by a nonconstant-coefficient Leray weight-floor argument. Finally, no stack-level or closed-support comparison with M_{6,6} is asserted. Thus the theorem is a conditional Tate-transfer result on the scheme Z-model, not a proof of the full codimension-13 contribution.

claims.statement: For the balanced scheme Z-model over Q, the invariant multiplicity M_[6] injects into the three constant-coefficient weight corners of S displayed in the theorem.
The sum M_[6]⊕M_[5,1] injects into the two constant-coefficient weight corners of the universal curve 𝒞 displayed in the theorem.
Hypothesis (H-S), namely Tate type for the degree 12, 14, and 16 constant-coefficient corners of S, implies that T_16(U)=T_16(Z)^{S_6} is a sum of Q(8).
Hypothesis (H-C), namely Tate type for the degree 14 and 16 constant-coefficient corners of 𝒞, implies that the [6]- and [5,1]-isotypic parts of T_16(Z) are sums of Q(8).
Neither (H-S) nor (H-C), nor Tate control of the other S_6-isotypic components, is established here; RED-0001 remains undischarged.

Control every S_6-isotypic multiplicity other than [6] and [5,1] by a constant Tate-coefficient comparison.

summary: The verified balanced geometry yields a precise constant-coefficient Tate-transfer theorem for the trivial and standard S_6 multiplicities. The proof uses rational finite-group transfer, two lowest-weight open-immersion injections, and the projective-bundle formula. It does not prove the required constant-coefficient Tate hypotheses on S or 𝒞, does not control the other S_6-isotypic components, and therefore does not resolve RED-0001.

theorem_scope.base: reduced locally Noetherian complex schemes in a smooth chart
excluded: comparison or Gysin map to M_{6,6}
theorem_scope.model: balanced Casnati–Ekedahl Abel–Jacobi reduced-support ordering model

theorem_statement: Sharp rational Tate-transfer criterion for the balanced Z-model. Let S be a connected reduced locally Noetherian complex scheme in a smooth chart of the balanced genus-six degree-four Hurwitz stack, with no component image contained in the type-(ii) locus. Let p:𝒞→S be the pulled-back universal curve, L=W_5⊗ω_p^{-1}, A=P_S(p_*L), U⊂A the reduced-support locus, and Z=Ord(U) its finite étale right S_6-ordering torsor. Write Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)=⊕_{λ⊢6} V_λ⊗M_λ. Then there are natural injections of pure weight-16 Hodge structures M_[6]→Gr^W_16 H_c^16(S;Q)⊕Gr^W_14 H_c^14(S;Q)(-1)⊕Gr^W_12 H_c^12(S;Q)(-2) and M_[6]⊕M_[5,1]→Gr^W_16 H_c^16(𝒞;Q)⊕Gr^W_14 H_c^14(𝒞;Q)(-1). Consequently, if Gr^W_{2j}H_c^{2j}(S;Q) is a sum of Q(-j) for j=6,7,8, then T_16(U)=T_16(Z)^{S_6} is a sum of Q(8); and if Gr^W_16 H_c^16(𝒞;Q) is a sum of Q(-8) and Gr^W_14 H_c^14(𝒞;Q) is a sum of Q(-7), then the [6]- and [5,1]-isotypic parts of T_16(Z):=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Z;Q) are sums of Q(8).
